correctness.rationale: Brown’s interval criterion is proved for nondecreasing integer sequences with initial zeros. Exact doubling gives \(H_{n+1}=H_n-\varepsilon_n\) where epsilon_n is the next binary digit. All future inequalities therefore hold exactly when the fractional part is dyadic of weight at most \(H_N\). The box-cover estimate and polynomial stratum counts are derived explicitly, with exact-integer corroboration over 965,528 sampled scales. The result is unrestricted for every finite prefix and all scales under eventual exact doubling.
